jobs.title: SVP, Actuary
jobs.description:
We are seeking a talented individual to join our Global Analytics & Advisory Actuarial team at Guy Carpenter. This role will be based in Toronto. This is a hybrid role that has a requirement of working at least three days a week in the office.

You will be a strategic partner with brokers and clients helping to find the solutions to client problems. The SVP, Actuary needs to be able to work hand in hand with the broking teams to ensure analytics resources are used appropriately, client needs are met, and GC Analytics is supporting and strengthening the relationship with the client.

We will count on you to:

Act independently to propose actuarial services and valuations to clients on their current and future needs to help them mitigate risk
Modify complex specialty models, and propose more value-added models to brokers and clients to assess their risk exposure and forecast risks, losses, and financial impact
Expand client services beyond reinsurance transactions to drive business development
Direct team to build complex specialty models to assess risk and develop pricing strategies for a range of risk exposures
Advise senior management on issues, progress, etc., regularly in order to ensure the reinsurance transaction process
Communicate strategically with brokers, re-insurers, and clients to anticipate clients’ needs and drive usage of reinsurance actuarial services

What you need to have:

minimum ACAS, preferably FCAS; at least 7-10 years in the industry
Bachelor’s degree in Actuarial Science, Economics, Math, Statistics, or related field
Pricing, valuation and/or capital modeling experience
Strong skills in Microsoft Office suite
Visualization skills – Power BI, Tableau or similar
Excellent communication skills; verbal and written
Coding experience in programming languages (i.e. Alteryx, R, Python, VBA, SQL)
Comfortable working in interactive teams with brokers and clients
Ability to lead day-to-day parts of the project and make decisions to keep projects moving forward
Strong problem-solving skills

What makes you stand out:

Reinsurance experience
French Canadian fluency

Why join our team:

We help you be your best through professional development opportunities, interesting work and supportive leaders.
We foster a vibrant and inclusive culture where you can work with talented colleagues to create new solutions and have impact for colleagues, clients and communities.
Our scale enables us to provide a range of career opportunities, as well as benefits and rewards to enhance your well-being.

Marsh (NYSE: MRSH) is a global leader in risk, reinsurance and capital, people and investments, and management consulting, advising clients in 130 countries. With annual revenue of over $27 billion and more than 95,000 colleagues, Marsh helps build the confidence to thrive through the power of perspective. For more information, visit marsh.com, or follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Marsh is committed to providing an inclusive work environment. We aim to attract and retain the best, most qualified people and value colleagues of all backgrounds, without regard to age background, disability, ethnic origin, family duties, gender orientation or expression, marital status, nationality, parental status, personal or social status, political affiliation, race, religion and beliefs, sex/gender, sexual orientation or expression, skin color, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. If you require a specific accommodation because of a disability or medical need, please contact reasonableaccommodations@marsh.com.

Marsh is committed to hybrid work, which includes the flexibility of working remotely and the collaboration, connections and professional development benefits of working together in the office. All Marsh colleagues are expected to be in their local office or working onsite with clients at least three days per week. Office-based teams will identify at least one “anchor day” per week on which their full team will be together in person.

jobs.title: Director, Research Infrastructure
jobs.description:
Summary:

The director, research infrastructure provides strategic leadership and operational oversight for research infrastructure across the university. This position leads the planning, development, sustainability, and modernization of scientific equipment, facilities, and research infrastructure resources. Working closely with researchers, academic units, research centres, university leadership, and external partners, this role directs infrastructure investments, financial sustainability, facility operations, and long-term development initiatives. The director advances research capacity through effective stewardship of significant infrastructure assets, the coordination of infrastructure renewal and expansion projects, and the promotion of collaboration across the institution and beyond. This role also oversees infrastructure governance, reporting, and compliance, as well as the optimization of research equipment, facilities, and space utilization.

Duties and Responsibilities:

Oversees confidential strategic financial planning and sustainability initiatives for research infrastructure, including budgeting, fee structures, risk management approaches, revenue generation, and resource allocation.
Develops and implements long-term strategic research infrastructure plans aligned with university research priorities and future growth objectives.
Directs significant infrastructure investments, including the acquisition, replacement, renewal, and upgrading of scientific equipment and research facilities.
Manages the full employee lifecycle of direct reports, including hiring, professional development, mentoring, assigning workflow, and performance management.
Provides confidential strategic advice to senior leadership, committees, and stakeholders on infrastructure strategy, investment priorities, deviations from approved plans, and opportunities for expansion.
Supports and participates in securing matching funds and supports major research infrastructure purchases in collaboration with researchers, academic units, and faculties.
Directs and oversees the acquisition, allocation, and utilization of equipment and assets within core facilities, collaborating with laboratory and academic leaders to establish priorities and resolve competing operational needs.
Establishes and leads advisory committees to monitor strategic and financial plans and provide progress reporting through formal presentations and reports.
Supports the development of proposals for research infrastructure renewal, enhancement, and expansion in collaboration with researchers and advisory bodies.
Fosters interdisciplinary collaboration among university centres, research facilities, external partners, and other institutions to strengthen research capabilities and infrastructure capacity.
Leads the development and advancement of research facilities, including core research facilities.
Supports the operation of infrastructure units, including staffing, safety practices, client services, user fee schedules, maintenance activities, and operational planning.
Supports software systems used in the management of university research infrastructure in coordination with internal information technology partners.
Oversees financial tracking and reporting related to infrastructure purchases, operational expenditures, and revenue generated through equipment usage.
Maintains a current inventory of research equipment and infrastructure capacity and promotes access to this information across the research community.
Facilitates the redeployment of underutilized equipment to areas of need across campus or coordinates the appropriate disposal of assets.
Liaises with other universities, analytical facilities, and external organizations to share leading practices and strengthen infrastructure support.
Promotes the effective utilization of research space in collaboration with space management stakeholders.
Maintains institutional communication through annual reports, committee updates, strategic presentations, and other reporting activities.
Monitors compliance with applicable funding agencies, legislation, regulations, and university policies governing research infrastructure and operations.
Communicates and acts in a respectful and professional manner, collaborates effectively, abides by policy, contributes to a positive and productive work and learning environment, and models these behaviours across the institution.
Builds and leads diverse teams, champions inclusive leadership, and values different perspectives.
Engages in and supports the understanding and growth of employees with the frameworks, initiatives and activities relating to equity, diversity and inclusion and Indigenous engagement.
Sets and achieves actionable goals in alignment with Indigenous engagement and equity, diversity, and inclusion frameworks; addresses systemic inequities affecting underrepresented equity groups.
Undertakes related duties, as assigned, consistent with the nature of the position.

Qualifications:

A master's degree in physical sciences, engineering, physics, health sciences, or a related field; a doctoral degree is preferred.
Minimum of seven years of progressively responsible experience in research infrastructure management and operations.
Leadership experience with the ability to lead a team through challenging and complex situations and demonstrate leadership beyond reporting lines.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to influence, persuade, and drive action.
Ability to develop and progress strategy, initiatives, and innovative solutions.
Effective organizational and time management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities in an evolving environment.
Ability to build and maintain effective relationships, internally and externally, and build credibility and trust with diverse stakeholder groups.
Excellent analytical skills and ability to apply sound judgment in problem solving, evaluating courses of action, and making decisions on complex matters.

jobs.title: Head of Ad Sales, Canada
jobs.description:
About the Team

The Canada Ads Sales Team is responsible for the marketing vision, development, and growth of our advertising partnerships across CPG, New Verticals, and Restaurants. This team is rapidly growing, and is seeking additional team members to build an industry-leading ads and promotions business across DoorDash's Canada offerings. The growing DoorDash ads business has quickly become one of the best places for merchants and brands to market to local customers, in an ecosystem that benefits all parties.

About the Role

As the Senior Industry Manager, Canada, you will lead a team of Industry Managers, Account Executives and Post Sales Managers to build partnerships that create tangible value for both advertisers and DoorDash. In this role, you will manage the entire ads strategy across DoorDash Canada's CPG, New Verticals, and Restaurant advertiser base, and drive adoption of our growing ads and promotions offering. You will work cross-functionally with strategy, operations, marketing, analytics, and product to innovate on our future approach and solutions. You will report into the VP, North America and ANZ Ads Sales, in our Sales & Business Development organization.

You're excited about this opportunity because you will…

Successfully lead and develop a team of Industry Managers and sellers to consistently exceed business growth and product/feature adoption goals, grow advertiser value, and drive sustainable revenue for DoorDash across the Canadian market
Establish trusted senior-level customer relationships and deliver thought leadership both internally and externally across the CPG, New Verticals, and Restaurant industries in Canada
Represent advertiser needs to influence our Ads & Promos product roadmap and go-to-market strategy for the Canadian market
Develop sales materials and sales processes to enable future scale of the team and business across multiple verticals
Develop annual and quarterly sales plans and analyses to achieve ambitious goals and help customers meet their business and marketing objectives
Partner with US and global Ads Sales leadership to bring proven best practices to the Canadian market while adapting strategy to local market nuances
Lead short- and long-term business planning and sales forecasting to guide investment and resourcing decisions
Drive the development and implementation of AI tools and skills to continually improve team productivity and efficiency
Lead inspiring and actionable team meetings, trainings, and strategy sessions that keep the team aligned and motivated

We're excited about you because…

You have a minimum of 8+ years managing a sales team effectively and leading team performance management to meet and exceed goals. Overall industry experience of 15+ years
You are a consultative seller with significant experience in digital media or adjacent performance-oriented industries
You have built scaled Enterprise Ads businesses across CPG, New Verticals, and/or Restaurant clients in the past
You're an expert in using data and insights to inform recommendations, rooted in advertiser objectives and business priorities
You have a firm understanding of digital technologies within the marketing/media mix, and are savvy with digital advertising measurement from attribution to funnel metrics
You have strong written/verbal communication and presentation skills, and experience operating across several levels of an organization
You hire and recruit top and diverse talent to drive outsized impact on the business and contribute to DoorDash's culture
You have experience working directly with advertisers across CPG, New Verticals, and/or Restaurant categories
You have experience navigating the Canadian advertising landscape, including bilingual market and provincial considerations

Compensation

Actual compensation within the pay range listed below will be decided based on factors including, but not limited to, skills, prior relevant experience, and specific work location. Base salary is localized according to employee work location.

In addition to base salary, the compensation for this role includes opportunities for equity grants and sales commission. Talk to your recruiter for more information.

DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That's why we offer a comprehensive benefits package for all regular employees, that includes paid time off, paid parental leave, wellness benefit and several paid holidays.

Additionally, for full-time employees, DoorDash offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, disability and basic life insurance, an RRSP including an employer match, and a mental health program, among others.

To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here.

The base pay for this position ranges from our lowest geographical market up to our highest geographical market within British Columbia.

$159,300—$199,200 CAD

The total on-target earnings (base + commissions) for this position ranges from our lowest geographical market up to our highest geographical market within British Columbia.

$265,500—$332,000 CAD

About DoorDash

At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods.

DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees' happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

If you need any accommodations, please inform your recruiting contact upon initial connection.

Beware of recruitment scams: DoorDash, Deliveroo, and Wolt will never ask you to pay money or share sensitive financial information during hiring — learn more about our legitimate recruiting process at Recruitment Scam Awareness - DoorDash .

jobs.title: Director & Actuary, Corporate Development
jobs.description:
We are seeking a Director & Actuary to join Corporate Development, a highly dynamic team that partners across Manulife to evaluate and execute mergers, acquisitions, divestitures and other major strategic initiatives. The role combines actuarial and financial analysis with hands-on transaction execution, senior-level communication and cross-functional collaboration.

The opportunit
y

Corporate Development manages transactions on an end-to-end basis, including opportunity assessment, valuation, due diligence, deal structuring, negotiations, internal approvals, integration planning, closing and post-closing monitoring. The team acts as a catalyst, enabler and partner to help Manulife’s businesses execute their strategies through M&A as a complement to organic growth, while applying a disciplined process that identifies and manages key transaction risks.

Position Responsibilities

Conduct detailed company- and industry-specific research, including competitor and precedent transaction analysis and assessment of emerging competitive, capital, regulatory and accounting developments.
Prepare clear, concise reports and executive-ready presentations on industry, strategic and transaction-related topics.
Support the valuation of potential transactions, including reviewing calculations and analyzing period-over-period movements in capital, reserves, earnings projections and other transaction metrics.
Help manage transactions from initial evaluation through due diligence, negotiations, internal approvals and closing.
Partner with actuarial, finance, business and other functional teams to ensure valuation assumptions are appropriate and consistent with Manulife standards.
Assess the financial and strategic impact of potential transactions and strategic initiatives on Manulife’s operations, goals and objectives.
Communicate analytical conclusions and recommendations effectively in both written materials and oral presentations.
Contribute to a collaborative, team-oriented environment and support multiple concurrent priorities in a fast-moving setting.

Required Qualifications

Fellow of the Society of Actuaries (FSA) and/or Fellow of the Canadian Institute of Actuaries (FCIA), with 3+ years of progressive experience.
Strong analytical judgment, including the ability to interpret results, identify issues and coordinate timely, practical resolutions.
Ability to develop and assess pro forma financial statements on both a standalone and consolidated basis.
Strong understanding of financial statements, actuarial and valuation concepts, and transaction-related capital and reserve considerations.
Excellent organizational skills and flexibility to manage and prioritize several projects at the same time.
Strong interpersonal, communication and leadership skills, with the ability to work effectively across functions and levels of the organization.
Proactive and self-directed, with the ability to work independently and as part of a team of professionals.
Excellent written and visual presentation skills, particularly in Microsoft PowerPoint.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in corporate development, transaction advisory, actuarial finance, valuation, capital management or a related field.
Knowledge of insurance industry financial metrics, accounting standards, regulatory capital frameworks and performance evaluation tools.
Experience supporting due diligence, transaction modeling, deal structuring or integration planning.

W hat you bring

An ownership mindset and sound judgment when working through complex or ambiguous issues.
The ability to synthesize detailed actuarial, financial and strategic information into decision-useful insights.
A collaborative approach and confidence engaging with colleagues across businesses, functions and geographies.
High standards for accuracy, clarity and execution.

When You Join Our Team

We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.
We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.
As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.

The role being advertised is an existing vacancy.

Manulife Financial Corporation is a leading international financial services provider, helping people make their decisions easier and lives better. To learn more about us, visit https://www.manulife.com/en/about/our-story.html.

Manulife is an Equal Opportunity Employer

At Manulife/John Hancock, we embrace our diversity. We strive to attract, develop and retain a workforce that is as diverse as the customers we serve and to foster an inclusive work environment that embraces the strength of cultures and individuals. We are committed to fair recruitment, retention, advancement and compensation, and we administer all of our practices and programs without discrimination on the basis of race, ancestry, place of origin, colour, ethnic origin, citizenship, religion or religious beliefs, creed, sex (including pregnancy and pregnancy-related conditions), sexual orientation, genetic characteristics, veteran status, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital status, family status, disability, or any other ground protected by applicable law.

All information shared during the accommodation request process will be stored and used in a manner that is consistent with applicable laws and Manulife/John Hancock policies. To request a reasonable accommodation in the application process, contact hr@manulife.com.

jobs.title: Sector Director - Transit
jobs.description:
Overview

Colliers Project Leaders is a team committed to projects that make a difference in communities and for the people who live there.

We deliver capital project solutions that strengthen the built environment, partnering with our clients to bring critical infrastructure and complex building projects to life.

We’ve led over 20,000+ projects that:

Make cities more livable
Enhance workplaces
Create spaces people want to return to
Improve patient care
Deliver clean drinking water
Build a sustainable future

And so much more.

This is where you come in. We’re looking for people to join our team who are passionate about creating more sustainable, resilient and inclusive communities.

If this kind of work resonates with you, you’re in the right place

Your role

Lead with purpose. Innovate with impact.

We are looking for a Sector Director to join our Transit Team.

As a Sector Director, you will be the driving force behind identifying emerging market trends, shaping sector growth strategies, and accelerating business performance. Working across a dynamic matrix organization, you will partner with leaders and teams to transform insights into action, drive strategic priorities, and deliver on ambitious growth targets. This role combines sector leadership with project leadership, leveraging market opportunities, leading strategic pursuits, growing key client relationships, and ensuring the successful delivery of complex programs and projects.

As a recognized leader within your sector, you will develop and execute multi-year growth strategies that strengthen our market position and expand our client base. With a passion for operational excellence and successful project delivery, you will focus on deepening relationships within key strategic accounts while driving sustainable growth and profitability.

A natural collaborator, you thrive in a matrix environment and excel at aligning diverse stakeholders around common goals. You take ownership of organizational priorities and initiatives, translating them into meaningful results across teams and projects. Committed to continuous improvement, you actively seek innovative ways to enhance performance, strengthen operations, and create value for clients.

You will elevate our brand through thought leadership, industry engagement, and impactful client relationships, supported by a strong and growing network across the sector. If you’re ready to influence direction, strengthen market position, and make a visible impact, this is your opportunity to lead and grow at scale.

Responsibilities

Strategy

Act as an account manager on key strategic transit accounts, owning and achieving sector sales targets and account growth objectives.
Provide sector intelligence, market insights, and competitive analysis to support business planning, aligned with annual and multi-year growth objectives.
Identify emerging market trends, client challenges, and opportunities to expand market share.
Lead the technical, financial, and commercial input for strategic pursuits
Grow existing strategic client accounts through consultative relationship management.
Lead service line integration strategies that enhance value to clients.

Leadership

Demonstrate and act as a role model and influencer of our values and cultural behaviors
Develop new market opportunities for Colliers in the sector/account
Coach practitioners and leadership on sales strategies/tactics for the sector/account
Establish a strong brand presence for Colliers in the sector/account through authoring thought leadership, featuring in video spotlights, speaking at events and conferences nationally, and in existing sector accounts

Growth

Support sector/account pursuits as required by the Business Units, providing sector/account specific input and guidance on relevant trends, challenges, commercial strategy, and resourcing decisions
Identify opportunities, key accounts and clients and lead priority pursuits in collaboration with the Business Units
Support prospecting and competitive pursuits
Understand client buying behavior in the sector/account, with an ability to influence the procurement process to better position Colliers for success

Management

Lead sales planning for the sector/account, including service integration
Clarify and anticipate sector/account trends and articulate how they affect clients in the sector/account, both internally and externally, developing plans to capitalize on them or to pivot as necessary
Develop Sector/Account champions in the BUs to collaboratively grow talent and sector/account specific qualifications
Identify and work with key experts in BUs to support growth and build qualifications in the sector/account

Quality

Implement a culture of quality and adherence to our Sales system
Drive the integrity, accuracy, and consistency of all data assets within the sector/account to support informed decision making and operational excellence

Qualifications

A minimum of 10 years of experience as a practitioner (consultant or client side) including large multi-year projects and large programs of work having developed a unique technical capability or sector specialization recognized by the industry
Practiced in consultative sales; listening to clients, identifying opportunities, knowing what is required to close the sale, and seeing the sale through
Professional industry credentials relevant and specific to the sector are considered a strong asset
Is a known industry player and leader across the sector and is well connected with key organizations and clients (target and existing) in the sector
An established network of sector contacts and involvement with applicable sector industry and trade associations
Excellent verbal and written communication, facilitation and presentation skills for all levels of our clients and our own organization, including a proven ability to write winning proposals
The ability to project and maintain a positive outlook and demonstrate an energetic disposition
Willingness to travel as required

Expected Compensation: $126,376 – $173,677 per year (CAD)

This base salary range represents our good faith estimate at the time of posting and is based on market benchmarks and internal equity. The salary offered will be determined based on the successful candidate’s skills, experience, qualifications, and regional consideration. For most new hires, base salary falls between the minimum and the midpoint of the range. While offers above the midpoint are uncommon, they may be considered in exceptional circumstances. This approach helps ensure there is room for future salary growth within the role. In addition to base salary, the total rewards package may include annual bonus opportunities, employer RRSP contributions, comprehensive group benefits, including a Health Care Spending Account, and other benefits.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Don’t have every single qualification?
We know that some people are less likely to apply for a job unless they are a perfect match. At Colliers Project Leaders, we’re not looking for “perfect matches.” We’re looking to welcome people to our diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace. So, if you’re excited about this role but don’t have every single qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. Whether it’s this role or another one, you may be just the right candidate.

What You Can Expect

An opportunity to truly impact our communities
A flexible work environment
A comprehensive onboarding experience
Significant professional development, training, and a mentorship program
A paid volunteer day
An environment where people feel welcome, heard and included, regardless of their differences
And much more!

Join our team of difference-makers and help shape the growth of dynamic communities.

Disclaimer

Colliers Project Leaders is part of Colliers (NASDAQ, TSX: CIGI), a leading diversified professional services and investment management company, with more than 18,000 professionals operating in 63 countries.

We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from all qualified individuals. If you require accommodation throughout the recruitment process, please contact the assigned Talent Acquisition Business Partner.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) Use

We may use technology tools to assist in screening applications for keywords or qualifications. However, final selection decisions are made by our hiring team through human review and interviews.

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in Canada on a full-time basis. The employer will not sponsor applicants for work visas.

Practiced in consultative sales; listening to clients, identifying opportunities, knowing what is required to close the sale, and seeing the sale through
Professional industry credentials relevant and specific to the sector are considered a strong asset
Is a known industry player and leader across the sector and is well connected with key organizations and clients (target and existing) in the sector
An established network of sector contacts and involvement with applicable sector industry and trade associations
Excellent verbal and written communication, facilitation and presentation skills for all levels of our clients and our own organization, including a proven ability to write winning proposals
The ability to project and maintain a positive outlook and demonstrate an energetic disposition
Willingness to travel as required

Expected Compensation: $126,376 – $173,677 per year (CAD)

This base salary range represents our good faith estimate at the time of posting and is based on market benchmarks and internal equity. The salary offered will be determined based on the successful candidate’s skills, experience, qualifications, and regional consideration. For most new hires, base salary falls between the minimum and the midpoint of the range. While offers above the midpoint are uncommon, they may be considered in exceptional circumstances. This approach helps ensure there is room for future salary growth within the role. In addition to base salary, the total rewards package may include annual bonus opportunities, employer RRSP contributions, comprehensive group benefits, including a Health Care Spending Account, and other benefits.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.
